attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, giving his assessment of the order. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalisation keeps the hedge 'probably not enough'. 'Enforcement teeth' is a slight gloss on 'teeth' but a fair one. The claim mixes checkable description with a hedged judgment about whether the order goes far enough.

contract.note: The contract rightly treats the adequacy judgment as central and hedged, with no standard for 'enough'. Its plain_reading flag cannot be used to score the hedged part, since plain reading applies only to firm language. Axis not_applicable is appropriate.

evidence.note: The official White House fact sheet, dated 2023-10-30, records mandatory reporting under the Defense Production Act. That fits the descriptive 'some teeth' part. It is the government describing its own order and says nothing on whether the powers are enough.

reviews.rationale: The descriptive parts (broad scope, some binding requirements) match the fact sheet. But the claim's core is the hedged judgment 'probably not enough' teeth. Under policy, a probability-qualified claim is not scored, and no standard for 'enough' was given. Checking the descriptive parts alone cannot score the whole claim, so the outcome is not_adjudicable.
